items.rationale: Dismantling and refitting needed to place the drying equipment is covered under technical drying (5.2.7). Priced at the reference level of about 90.
Technical drying is covered (5.2.7), and 7 days is within the roughly two weeks of drying described. Priced at about 45 per day x 7.
7.4.4 pays surcharges only against an itemised list of materials; this surcharge is unexplained, and 7.4.3 treats consumables as included in the dryer charge.
Standard mineral-wool shell, which matches the 7.14(c) standard, used to reinstate the pipe bend. Priced at the reference level of about 26.
Under 5.2.1 debris removal is paid once and only the first charge counts; this drying invoice comes first. Risk remains that 7.4.4 blocks flat-rate items without an itemised list.
Re-levelling the substrate in the damage area is part of making good (5.2.6). Priced at about 38.
Substrate preparation in the damage area falls under making good. Estimated at roughly 30 per m² x 2.78.
Creating the service opening needed to reach the failed fitting is expressly covered under 5.2.6.
90x90 is within the 7.14(d) tile threshold. About 4 m² at the upper customary price for standard tiles.
These exceed the 90x90 threshold, and 3.5(f) gives no partial payment. They are also a designer upgrade (3.5(a)) and duplicate the tiling in line 9 (3.5(d)).
Standard sanitary silicone joints to the reinstated tiling. Priced at about 13 per m x 3.6.
This is the only travel charge on the tiler's document, so it is paid once under 7.4.2. Priced at about 82, as in case 46.
Tiling labour is covered at customary local rates. Priced as in case 46 at about 90 per hour x 14.
Opening up within the basement damage area is covered (5.2.6). Combines the case 46 drywall and insulation removal levels.
Removing damp plaster in the basement damage area is opening up/making good. Priced near the case 46 level.
The attic is outside the damage area and the work is unrelated, so 3.5(b) and 7.1.5 exclude it.
This duplicates the disposal already charged by the drying contractor; 5.2.1 and 3.5(d) reimburse only the first charge.
